subject: Prompt set collection & model fit follow-up — ACME
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Prompt set & model fit — Redwood evals

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo today — that was really helpful. As promised, attached is a first pass of our prompt samples (acme_prompt_samples.csv). High-level notes:

- File contains ~120 prompts across 3 buckets: happy-path, edge-cases (long threads, nested quotes, mixed languages), and redaction-required (SSNs, account numbers, PHI-like examples).
- Our primary goal: replace current rule-based summarizer with an LLM-powered summary + action extraction. Latency target: median < 300ms per request for short inputs; we're ok batching for longer jobs.
- Success metrics: F1 on extraction >= 0.85, and subjective summary quality >= internal baseline.

Could you share:
1) Recommended model(s) to start evals with (accuracy vs latency tradeoffs).
2) Any immediate redaction guidance we should apply to the samples before you run them.
3) Timeline to get back with initial benchmark numbers.

Looping in Priya on the prompt file — she owns the dataset.

Thanks,
Jordan
Account Tech Lead, ACME Corp

Attachments: acme_prompt_samples.csv (CSV, 120 rows, columns: prompt_id, category, prompt_text, expected_entities)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Jun 2026 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Prompt set & model fit — Redwood evals

Hi Jordan / Priya — great to get the samples, thanks. I pulled the file and kicked off an initial pass. Quick answers up front, then next steps: 

1) Recommended starting models: 
- Redwood-13B-v1 (8-bit quant) — best accuracy/latency balance for extraction + summarization.
- Redwood-7B-fast — good low-latency option for short conversational inputs and lower cost.
- Redwood-RT-1.3B — experimental/baseline for throughput testing if you need a very low-cost tier.

2) Redaction guidance (please apply before we share any production logs):
- Replace exact identifiers (SSNs, full account numbers) with tokens like <REDACTED_ACCOUNT_ID>.
- For free-text PHI, remove patient names and replace with <REDACTED_NAME> and keep enough context for the model to infer roles where needed.
- Flag and separate very long transcripts (>8k chars) — we'll run those in a batched offline job.

3) Timeline: I ran a quick internal benchmark and attached a short PDF with preliminary numbers (benchmark_results_v2.pdf). Full eval set (all 120 prompts, cross-model, 3 seeds) will take ~3 business days to complete and I'll share the dashboard link.

Observations from the quick pass:
- A handful of prompts in the edge-cases bucket contain nested e-mail quoting patterns that cause hallucinated extractions. We should add negative examples (where the model should return no entities) to capture that behavior.
- Some expected_entities values look noisy — will need a small verification pass from Priya to make sure our scoring is accurate.

Next steps:
- Priya: can you confirm expected_entities for the 14 flagged rows?
- Jordan: any specific latency SLA or throughput targets beyond median <300ms?
- I'll run the full sweep, post results to https://redwood.ai/evals/ACME-912/perf, and then schedule a 30-min sync to review model-fit and pricing tradeoffs.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: benchmark_results_v2.pdf (summary of quick-pass numbers)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Follow-up: Prompt set & model fit — ACME (prompt set attached)

Forwarding ACME's samples and my notes — see thread below. Internal asks: 

- Rishi: pricing/contract note — ACME is sensitive to per-token costs. If we recommend Redwood-13B-v1 quant as primary, can you draft a quick cost delta (steady-state monthly for 100k tpm) and a potential discount ladder? Attach to the deal record (DEAL-ACME-00912) in HubSpot.

- Dev: can you review the prompt file for edge-case tokenization issues? A few prompts exceed 4k tokens; we should normalize and categorize which ones are for online vs. offline batch. Also check content for accidental PII left unredacted (we flagged ~12 rows).

- Engineering concern to flag: model rollout/quality regression — ACME wants stable outputs. Please propose a monitoring plan (prompt-set based regression alerts + periodic snapshot evals). We should recommend a canary rollout and rollback window in the proposal.

Thanks for the ping — quick summary of what I ran and recommendations: 

1) Prompt sanitation & tokenization:
- Verified CSV parsing; 12 rows contain clear PII (full account numbers / SSN-like strings). I redacted locally and attached a redacted sample set to the drive link.
- ~9 prompts exceed 4k tokens when expanded with context — recommend those be marked for offline batch processing. We can auto-truncate system messages + preserve last 1.5k tokens for online mode.

2) Model recommendations (engineering lens):
- Start with Redwood-13B-v1 (8-bit quant) for accuracy-sensitive evals.
- Redwood-7B-fast for latency-sensitive paths (short conversational summaries).
- For scale testing, run Redwood-RT-1.3B for throughput and to validate cost assumptions.

3) Quality regression / monitoring plan:
- Baseline: run nightly snapshot evals on the accepted prompt-set (50 deterministic seeds) and compute entity-extraction F1 + summary ROUGE-L.
- Alerting: regression alert if F1 drops > 3% absolute or ROUGE-L drops > 4 points.
- Canary: 1% production traffic on new model version for 24h with automatic rollback on regressions.

4) Next steps & timeline:
- I'll push a sanitized prompt set and tokenization report to the drive by EOD Friday.
- Marissa: if we want, I can spin up the two recommended variants and post the per-model perf numbers to the eval dashboard in ~48 hours.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Software Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
